panels.description: This lists every recorded index generation, newest first, with its state, size, and completion times. A failed state or missing completion time after work stops needs investigation; retired generations remain listed. Follow docs/runbooks/observability.md §3.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT split_part(gen_id, '__', 2) AS lockfile, split_part(gen_id, '__', 3) AS space, state, bytes, created_at, lexical_built_at, dense_built_at, built_at, promoted_at
FROM index_generations
ORDER BY created_at DESC, gen_id

panels.title: Generations

panels.description: This counts documents by processing status and court in the newest report of each generation that is not retired. Failed documents or a ready count that stops growing during a build need investigation. Follow docs/runbooks/observability.md §3.

targets.rawSql:
WITH newest AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (r.gen_id) r.gen_id, r.courts
    FROM build_reports r
    JOIN index_generations g USING (gen_id)
    WHERE g.state <> 'retired'
    ORDER BY r.gen_id, r.written_at DESC
)
SELECT split_part(r.gen_id, '__', 2) AS lockfile, court.key AS court,
       distribution.key AS status, distribution.value::bigint AS documents
FROM newest r
CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_each(r.courts) AS court
CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_each_text(court.value->'by_status') AS distribution
ORDER BY lockfile DESC, court, status

panels.title: Documents by status

panels.description: This counts documents by the source column their text came from and by court in the newest report of each generation that is not retired. Unexpected missing sources or a changed distribution can explain parsing failures. Follow docs/runbooks/observability.md §3.

targets.rawSql:
WITH newest AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (r.gen_id) r.gen_id, r.courts
    FROM build_reports r
    JOIN index_generations g USING (gen_id)
    WHERE g.state <> 'retired'
    ORDER BY r.gen_id, r.written_at DESC
)
SELECT split_part(r.gen_id, '__', 2) AS lockfile, court.key AS court,
       distribution.key AS text_source, distribution.value::bigint AS documents
FROM newest r
CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_each(r.courts) AS court
CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_each_text(court.value->'by_text_source') AS distribution
ORDER BY lockfile DESC, court, text_source

panels.title: Documents by precedential status

panels.description: This counts failed documents by reason and court in the newest report of each generation that is not retired. A court with no failures has no row; listed failures identify the processing problems to investigate. Follow docs/runbooks/observability.md §3.

targets.rawSql:
WITH newest AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (r.gen_id) r.gen_id, r.courts
    FROM build_reports r
    JOIN index_generations g USING (gen_id)
    WHERE g.state <> 'retired'
    ORDER BY r.gen_id, r.written_at DESC
)
SELECT split_part(r.gen_id, '__', 2) AS lockfile, court.key AS court,
       distribution.key AS reason, distribution.value::bigint AS documents
FROM newest r
CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_each(r.courts) AS court
CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_each_text(court.value->'by_failure_reason') AS distribution
ORDER BY lockfile DESC, court, reason

panels.title: Failures by reason

panels.description: This shows each court's staged and recorded counts, ready and failed documents, accounted gate, anchored documents, and agreement counts in the newest report of each generation that is not retired. A false pass means fewer documents were recorded than staged; missing agreement figures remain blank, while unexpectedly low anchor or agreement counts need investigation. Follow docs/runbooks/observability.md §3.

targets.rawSql:
WITH newest AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (r.gen_id) r.gen_id, r.courts, r.gates
    FROM build_reports r
    JOIN index_generations g USING (gen_id)
    WHERE g.state <> 'retired'
    ORDER BY r.gen_id, r.written_at DESC
)
SELECT split_part(r.gen_id, '__', 2) AS lockfile, court.key AS court,
       (r.gates->'accounted'->court.key->>'staged')::bigint AS staged,
       (r.gates->'accounted'->court.key->>'recorded')::bigint AS recorded,
       (r.gates->'accounted'->court.key->>'ready')::bigint AS ready,
       (r.gates->'accounted'->court.key->>'failed')::bigint AS failed,
       (r.gates->'accounted'->court.key->>'pass')::boolean AS pass,
       (court.value->'anchors'->>'anchored')::bigint AS anchored,
       (court.value->'agreement'->>'agreed')::bigint AS agreed,
       (court.value->'agreement'->>'gideon_pairs')::bigint AS gideon_pairs,
       (court.value->'agreement'->>'map_pairs')::bigint AS map_pairs
FROM newest r
CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_each(r.courts) AS court
ORDER BY lockfile DESC, court

panels.title: Anchors, agreement, and the accounted gate

panels.description: This shows command and indexing times, failure details, and whether the newest report of each generation that is not retired covers a whole build. Large run or indexing times can mean slow work; a failed stage names where it stopped. Lifecycle is the span from creation to built, including gaps between commands, and is never a build duration. Follow docs/runbooks/observability.md §3.

targets.rawSql:
WITH newest AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (r.gen_id) r.gen_id, r.written_at, r.failed_stage, r.failure_reason, r.wall_clock
    FROM build_reports r
    JOIN index_generations g USING (gen_id)
    WHERE g.state <> 'retired'
    ORDER BY r.gen_id, r.written_at DESC
)
SELECT split_part(gen_id, '__', 2) AS lockfile, split_part(gen_id, '__', 3) AS space, written_at AS report_at, failed_stage, failure_reason,
       (wall_clock->>'run_seconds')::bigint AS run_seconds,
       (wall_clock->>'lexical_seconds')::bigint AS lexical_seconds,
       (wall_clock->>'dense_seconds')::bigint AS dense_seconds,
       (wall_clock->>'lifecycle_seconds')::bigint AS lifecycle_seconds,
       (wall_clock->>'whole_build')::boolean AS whole_build
FROM newest
ORDER BY split_part(gen_id, '__', 2) DESC, gen_id

panels.title: Build wall clock

panels.description: This shows recorded dense indexing progress for each generation that is not retired. Written is Copied plus Embedded, and Tokens/s is Tokens divided by the seconds of the Embedding column; missing keys and a rate without positive seconds remain blank. A growing waiting queue with counts that stop advancing can mean a stalled build. Follow docs/runbooks/observability.md §3.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT split_part(gen_id, '__', 2) AS lockfile, split_part(gen_id, '__', 3) AS space,
       (counts->>'dense_scope')::bigint AS scope,
       (counts->>'dense_copied')::bigint + (counts->>'dense_embedded')::bigint AS written,
       (counts->>'dense_present')::bigint AS present,
       (counts->>'dense_copied')::bigint AS copied,
       (counts->>'dense_embedded')::bigint AS embedded,
       (counts->>'dense_tokens')::bigint AS tokens,
       (counts->>'dense_requests')::bigint AS requests,
       (counts->>'dense_seconds')::bigint AS seconds,
       (counts->>'dense_indexed')::bigint AS indexed,
       (counts->>'dense_tokens')::numeric / NULLIF((counts->>'dense_seconds')::numeric, 0) AS tokens_per_second
FROM index_generations
WHERE state <> 'retired'
ORDER BY created_at DESC, gen_id

panels.title: Embedding progress

panels.description: This shows the embedding server's waiting queue at each step's maximum and the mean number of requests executing inside the engine over the panel's rate window, computed from finished requests' inference time. In inference is a mean, not a count, and can read below one between bursts. A queue that keeps growing means work is arriving faster than it is served. The server's own running gauge reads 0 at every scrape for an embedding model, so it is not drawn. This panel is empty on a no-GPU host, where no embedding server runs. Follow docs/runbooks/observability.md §3.
panels.title: Embedding requests waiting and in inference

panels.description: This shows tokens processed per second by the embedding server over the panel's rate window. Low throughput while requests wait can mean the build is slowing. This panel is empty on a no-GPU host, where no embedding server runs, and while nothing embeds in the range. Follow docs/runbooks/observability.md §3.
panels.title: Tokens embedded per second

panels.description: This shows successful embedding requests per second over the panel's rate window. A falling rate with waiting work can mean requests are stalled or failing. This panel is empty on a no-GPU host, where no embedding server runs, and while nothing embeds in the range. Follow docs/runbooks/observability.md §3.
panels.title: Embedding requests per second

panels.description: This shows the median and 95th percentile embedding request times from the panel's rate window over the server's latency buckets. Rising times mean requests take longer to finish. This panel is empty on a no-GPU host, where no embedding server runs, and while nothing embeds in the range. Follow docs/runbooks/observability.md §3.
panels.title: Embedding request latency

panels.description: This shows the lexical store's heap use against its dashed heap limit and the vector store's resident and allocated memory, from their own measurements. Heap use close to its limit or sustained memory growth can slow indexing or exhaust memory. Follow docs/runbooks/observability.md §3.
panels.title: Store memory

panels.description: This shows points and vectors in each collection from the vector store's own measurements. Counts should advance during a dense build; unexpected missing collections or counts that stop growing while work waits need investigation. Follow docs/runbooks/observability.md §3.
panels.title: Collections

panels.description: This shows lexical indexing work beside each vector collection's update queue and running optimizations. A growing update queue with no progress can mean a store cannot keep up. Follow docs/runbooks/observability.md §3.
panels.title: Store work in flight

panels.description: This shows the lexical store's indexing rate per index over the panel's rate window, excluding dot-prefixed system indexes and counting primary shards. Each index is named by its generation's lockfile; a low rate while build work waits can mean indexing is stalled. Follow docs/runbooks/observability.md §3.
panels.title: Documents indexed per second

panels.description: This shows whether lexical indexing is throttled, measured by the lexical store. Persistent throttling can mean the store cannot keep up and can slow indexing. Follow docs/runbooks/observability.md §3.
panels.title: Lexical indexing throttled

panels.description: This shows waiting jobs per worker queue from the worker's measurements. Known queues remain visible at zero; a queue that grows while running jobs make no progress needs investigation. Follow docs/runbooks/observability.md §3.
panels.title: Worker jobs waiting

panels.description: This shows running jobs per worker queue from the worker's measurements. Known queues remain visible at zero; running jobs that make no progress while work waits need investigation. Follow docs/runbooks/observability.md §3.
panels.title: Worker jobs running

panels.description: This shows the worker's own heartbeat age and configured job slots. A stale heartbeat can mean the worker stopped; too few slots for sustained waiting work can limit progress. The worker's Overview tile carries its liveness page. Follow docs/runbooks/observability.md §3.
panels.title: Worker heartbeat and slots
